newsitem.title: BENIN: Benin puts 97/98 seed cotton crop at 450,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Benin puts 97/98 seed cotton crop at 450,000 T.

text.p: Benin's seed cotton harvest will total 450,000 tonnes for the 1997/98 season (March-Feb), a state cotton marketing agency official forecast Thursday.
The 1996/97 season was also originally forecast to produce 450,000 tonnes but came in at 230,000 tonnes after 349,000 tonnes in the previous season despite unfavourable weather.
Around 450,000 hectares had been planted with cotton since March, the official told Reuters.
The official from Sonapra said the farmgate price would remain unchanged at 200 CFA francs a kilo.
One industry manager said it was too early too make predictions after last year's shortfall.
Planters say the productive Zou-Nord region and others had experienced rain shortages but planting had nevertheless been completed by June.
Benin cotton harvests usually get underway from November before factory processing in January and marketing up to March.
Rural agencies said they would urge farmers to adopt more intensive farming practices to allow more production without increases in the overall area planted.
